item.title: Agu Pork — Guide
item.description: Agu (or Agu) is Okinawa’s prized native breed of black pig, and its pork is considered a premium local delicacy. Descended from pigs brought to the Ryukyu Islands centuries ago, the Agu is a small, slow-growing and relatively rare breed, which nearly died out before being carefully revived. Its meat is celebrated for exceptionally fine marbling, a low melting point that gives the fat a melt-in-the-mouth quality, and a distinctive sweetness and umami-rich, tender texture with none of the heaviness of ordinary pork.

item.title: Tokushima Ramen: Dark Pork Broth and Raw Egg — Guide
item.description: Tokushima ramen is one of Japan’s most distinctive regional ramen styles, immediately recognisable by its rich, dark brown broth. Made from a pork-bone base seasoned heavily with soy sauce (and sometimes a tonkotsu-shoyu blend), the soup is deep, savoury and slightly sweet. The signature topping is not the usual sliced chashu but sweet-and-savoury simmered pork belly (butabara), rich and glossy, along with bean sprouts and spring onion — and, most famously, a raw egg cracked straight onto the hot noodles, which you mix in to enrich and mellow the broth, sukiyaki-style.
